body.p: I. Summary oSVG {EMBED HERE} 0.0830.077of the Office Action
In the Office Action dated August 1, 2024, the Examiner:
(i) rejected claims 1-20 under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as allegedly being directed to non- statutory subject matter;

(ii) rejected claims 1-20 on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 1-4, 7, 14, and 15 of U.S. Pat. No. 11,642,043; (iii) rejected claims 1-20 on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 1-4, 7, 13, and 14 of U.S. Pat. No. 11,957,448;
(v) indicated that claims 1-20 would be allowable if the 35 U.S.C. § 101 and Double Patenting rejections were overcome.
Claims 1-20 are pending. In this response, Applicant has (a) amended claims 1-2, 4-7, and 15, (b) canceled claims 8-14, and (c) added claims 21-27. After entry of this amendment,
III. Examiner Interview
Applicant's representative would like to thank Examiner Vanchy for the telephonic interview on January 30, 2025. During the interview, the participants discussed proposed
amendments to independent claims 1, 8, and 15 in view of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 101.
The Examiner agreed that the proposed amendments to claims 1 and 15 would overcome the current rejections. No agreement was reached with respect to the proposed amendment to
independent claim 8.
IV. Response to the Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. § 101
As indicated above, the Office rejected claims 1-20 under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as allegedly being directed to non-statutory subject matter.
In this response, Applicant has amended independent claims 1 and 15 as discussed during the interview, and canceled independent claim 8. Accordingly, as agreed during the interview,
amended claims 1-7 and 15-20 are directed to statutory subject matter.
V. Response to the Double Patenting Rejection
As indicated above, the Office (i) rejected claims 1-20 on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 1-4, 7, 14, and 15 of U.S. Pat. No.

11,642,043, (ii) rejected claims 1-20 on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 1-4, 7, 13, and 14 of U.S. Pat. No. 11,957,448, and (iii) rejected claims 1-3, 8-10, and 15-17 on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as allegedly being
unpatentable over claims 1, 2, and 4 of U.S. Pat. No. 10,987,024.
To overcome this rejection, a Terminal Disclaimer is submitted herewith. This Terminal Disclaimer should not be construed as an admission to the merits of the nonstatutory double
patenting rejections pursuant to Quad Environmental Technologies Corp. v. Union Sanitary
District, 946 F.2d 870 (Fed. Cir. 1991); see also MPEP § 804.02.
In view of the Terminal Disclaimer, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection of claims 1-3, 5, 11-13, and 15-17 on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting.
VI. Allowable Subject Matter
As indicated above, the Office indicated that claims 1-20 would be allowable if the 35 U.S.C. § 101 and Double Patenting rejections were overcome. Applicant thanks the Examiner
for the indication of allowable subject matter.
VII. Conclusion
Applicant respectfully submits that the claims are allowable. Thus, Applicant
respectfully requests favorable action.
Should the Examiner wish to discuss this case with the undersigned, the Examiner is invited to call the undersigned at (312) 913-2125.
Respectfully submitted,
Date: February 3, 2025 By: /Jason Krav/
Jason Kray
